q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT A.VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS CNT FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID) A WHERE A.CNT>=2 ORDER BY ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT A.VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM ( SELECT VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID, COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) AS CNT FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID) A WHERE A.CNT>=2 ORDER BY ID
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 1001, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (2, 102, 1001, '2023-01-02');
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, and then filters for viewers who have viewed more than one distinct article on that specific date. Q2 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, counts the distinct articles each viewer has viewed on that date, and then filters for viewers who have viewed two or more distinct articles on that date. The key difference is that Q1 does not consider the total count of distinct articles across all dates, while Q2 does.
counterexample_dsp: A viewer who has viewed two distinct articles on two different dates.
